mainTopic: Clearing space on שבת for guests and Torah study: the storeroom rules, piled grain and מוקצה, the limits on clearing, and the greatness of הכנסת אורחין
overview: This amud finishes explaining the משנה about clearing baskets of produce on שבת to make room for guests or for a בית המדרש. The גמרא says 'four or five' is loose speech. It also says 'not the storeroom' means you may not empty the whole storeroom, in case you fill in holes in the floor. The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who has no מוקצה prohibition. Two ברייתות follow. The first is about starting a storeroom and making a path with one's feet. The second is about piled grain, where the names are swapped so that רבי שמעון is the lenient one. Piled grain is defined as a לתך. Next come two איבעיות. The first asks whether the limit is about fewer trips or lighter loads, and the answer is fewer trips. The second asks whether the amount grows with the number of guests: stories about רבי and רבי חייא clearing a whole field show that it does. A proof that one man may clear for everyone is pushed off. The amud closes with praise of הכנסת אורחין, which is compared to the בית המדרש and even to greeting the שכינה. It also gives רבי יוחנן's list of six מצוות whose fruits are eaten in this world. A challenge to that list from a משנה is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: Four or five is just a loose expression
steps.stepSummary: The number 'four or five' in the משנה is ordinary speech, not an exact limit, so even more baskets may be cleared.
steps.simpleTranslation: As people say. And if he wants, he may clear even a lot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer about the number in the משנה. 'Four and five' is just how people talk, so a person may clear even more baskets if he needs to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said one may clear 'four or five baskets,' which sounds like a fixed limit. The גמרא explains that this is loose everyday speech for 'a few.' Since the number is not a real limit, there is no maximum.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'four or five' as a real maximum. The גמרא says it is only a figure of speech, so more may be cleared.

phrases.english: as people say,
phrases.notes: The number in the משנה is loose, everyday phrasing.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בָּעֵי אֲפִילּוּ טוּבָא נָמֵי מְפַנִּין.
phrases.english: and if he wants, he may clear even many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer earlier about the number of baskets in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה sets an exact limit of four or five baskets.
steps.terutzMaskana: The number is colloquial, so one may clear as many as needed.

steps.title: What does 'but not the storeroom' mean?
steps.stepSummary: If there is no limit on the number of baskets, the גמרא asks what the משנה's exclusion of the storeroom means.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'but not the storeroom' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move by asking what the משנה means by 'but not the storeroom.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that one may clear as many baskets as needed. So what is excluded when the משנה says 'not the storeroom'? The question points to a seeming conflict between unlimited clearing and a ban on the storeroom.

keyTerms.meaning: Storeroom, a large stockpile of produce

phrases.english: And what is 'but not the storeroom'?
phrases.notes: Quoting the end of the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 1. Since clearing is unlimited, the meaning of the storeroom exclusion needs explaining.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is forbidden regarding the storeroom?

steps.title: You may start the storeroom but not finish it
steps.stepSummary: One may not empty the whole storeroom, lest he level holes in the floor. Beginning to take from it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: That he should not finish all of it, lest he come to level holes. But he may begin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ban is only on emptying the entire storeroom. Starting to take from it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the floor is fully exposed, a person might fill in its pits and holes to even it out. That is a forbidden act of fixing the ground on שבת. As long as he only takes part, the floor is not exposed and this worry does not arise.

keyTerms.meaning: To level (fill in) holes in the floor

phrases.english: that he should not finish all of it,
lest he come to level holes.
phrases.notes: With the floor exposed, he might fill in pits, which is forbidden repair work.

phrases.english: But he may begin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exclusion forbids finishing the storeroom, because of leveling holes. Beginning is allowed.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who has no מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the author of the משנה as רבי שמעון, since he does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is it? It is רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies whose opinion the משנה follows: רבי שמעון, who does not forbid moving set-aside items (מוקצה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain stored away in a storeroom could be seen as set aside and off-limits on שבת. Since the משנה lets one begin taking from a storeroom, it must follow רבי שמעון, who has no such prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Set-aside items, forbidden to move on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה allows clearing even many baskets and beginning a storeroom, but not emptying it, because of leveling holes. It follows רבי שמעון, who has no מוקצה.

phrases.english: And who is it? It is Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: Identifying the author of the משנה.

phrases.english: who does not hold of set-aside (muktzeh).
phrases.notes: That is why beginning a storeroom is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the discussion of the משנה by identifying its author.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who rejects מוקצה, so taking from a storeroom is permitted.

steps.title: A ברייתא: do not start a storeroom, but make a path
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one may not begin a storeroom for the first time, but may make a path in it to go in and out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may not begin a storeroom for the first time, but he makes a path in it so he can enter and exit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It forbids starting a storeroom on שבת but allows making a path through it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא seems stricter than our משנה, which allowed beginning a storeroom. It also adds a new allowance: making a path. That allowance will be questioned next.

keyTerms.meaning: For the first time, at the start

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא.

phrases.english: one may not begin in a storeroom for the first time,
phrases.notes: A storeroom never used before may not be opened on שבת.

phrases.english: but he makes a path in it
so that he may enter and exit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אֵין מַתְחִילִין בָּאוֹצָר תְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא on the topic of the storeroom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not begin a storeroom for the first time on שבת, but may make a path to enter and exit.

steps.title: Making a path contradicts 'not beginning'
steps.stepSummary: Making a path means moving baskets, which seems to be the very 'beginning' the ברייתא just forbade.
steps.simpleTranslation: He makes a path in it?! But you said one may not begin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from within. If one may not begin a storeroom, how can one make a path in it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: To clear a path you must move baskets, and that counts as starting the storeroom. So the first half of the ברייתא seems to contradict its second half.

phrases.english: He makes a path in it?!
But you said one may not begin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The allowance to make a path in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Making a path requires moving baskets, which is beginning the storeroom, and that was just forbidden.

steps.title: The path is made with the feet
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means he makes a path by pushing aside with his feet as he walks in and out, not by moving baskets with his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: he makes a path with his feet as he enters and as he exits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. The path is made by shifting things with one's feet while walking, not by lifting with one's hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving things with the feet as you walk is an indirect, unusual way of moving them. It does not count as properly 'beginning' the storeroom. So the ban on beginning refers to moving by hand, and the path is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying
As he enters and as he exits

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: Reinterpreting the ברייתא.

phrases.english: he makes a path in it with his feet
as he enters and as he exits.
phrases.notes: Incidentally, while walking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Making a path means moving baskets by hand, which would be beginning the storeroom.
steps.terutzMaskana: The path is made with the feet while walking, which is not considered beginning.

steps.title: A ברייתא on piled grain: started before שבת or not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records an opinion that piled grain may be used on שבת only if one began taking from it before שבת, while another תנא permits it in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Piled grain, if he began taking from it on ערב שבת, he may use it on שבת. If not, he may not. These are the words of רבי שמעון. רבי אחא permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about piled grain. As written, רבי שמעון is strict unless the pile was started before שבת, and רבי אחא is lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An untouched pile seems set aside, like מוקצה. Once it was started before שבת, it shows the owner intends to use it. The names as written will soon be questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: To take what one needs, to supply oneself

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Piled grain,
when he began taking from it on Shabbat eve,
it is permitted to supply himself from it on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אָסוּר לְהִסְתַּפֵּק מִמֶּנָּה בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: and if not, it is forbidden to supply himself from it on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: An untouched pile is treated as set aside.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: That's how the words read at first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha permits.
phrases.notes: In all cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about piled grain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As written, רבי שמעון permits piled grain only if it was begun before שבת, and רבי אחא permits it always.

steps.title: The opposite: רבי שמעון is the lenient one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this is backwards, since רבי שמעון is known to be lenient about מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא protests that the ברייתא has the opinions reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה, as we saw in step 4. So it makes no sense that he would be the strict one here. The attribution clashes with his known view.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary! (literally, 'toward the other side')

phrases.english: On the contrary!
phrases.notes: This is the reverse of רבי שמעון's known view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the attribution of opinions in the ברייתא of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The names attached to each opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון rejects מוקצה, so he should be the lenient one, not the strict one.

steps.title: Swap the names: רבי אחא is strict, רבי שמעון permits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the ברייתא: the strict view belongs to רבי אחא, and רבי שמעון permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: These are the words of רבי אחא, and רבי שמעון permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא by switching the names so they match רבי שמעון's known leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself stays the same, and only the attributions are reversed. Now רבי אחא requires that the pile was started before שבת, and רבי שמעון permits in all cases, consistent with his rejection of מוקצה.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is fixing the wording here.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Acha,
phrases.notes: The strict view.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon permits.
phrases.notes: Consistent with having no מוקצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 9 by emending the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון is strict about untouched piled grain.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אחא is strict, and רבי שמעון permits in all cases.
steps.whatToRemember: After the correction, רבי שמעון permits using piled grain on שבת even if it was not started before שבת, because he does not hold of מוקצה.

steps.title: How big is 'piled grain'? A לתך
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the amount that counts as 'piled grain' is a לתך (half a כור).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: How much is the measure of piled grain? A לתך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a teaching that gives the size of grain that counts as a 'piled grain' storeroom: a לתך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This defines when the rules about piled grain apply. A smaller amount is not considered a stockpile.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a כור (15 סאה), a large dry measure

phrases.english: It was taught: How much is the measure of piled grain?
A half-kor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term 'piled grain' from the ברייתא of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Piled grain means at least a לתך.

steps.title: רב נחומי בר זכריה asks אביי the size
steps.stepSummary: רב נחומי בר זכריה asks אביי what the measure of piled grain is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחומי בר זכריה asked אביי: The measure of piled grain, how much is it?
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא asks אביי for the measure of piled grain. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question shows this measure was something people wanted confirmed by a teacher. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה מֵאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Nechumi bar Zecharya asked of Abaye:
The measure of piled grain, how much is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה מֵאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks again about the measure stated in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum amount that counts as piled grain.

steps.title: אביי answers: they already said a לתך
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers by citing the known teaching that the measure of piled grain is a לתך.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They already said, the measure of piled grain is a לתך.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers by quoting the earlier teaching: a לתך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי adds no new number. He confirms the ברייתא from step 11 as the accepted measure.
steps.whatToRemember: Piled grain counts as a storeroom stockpile when it is at least a לתך (half a כור), as taught in the ברייתא and confirmed by אביי.

phrases.english: He said to him: They have said:
The measure of piled grain is a half-kor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 12.

steps.title: Is the limit about fewer trips or lighter loads?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה's 'four or five baskets' limits the number of trips or the weight carried each time.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: When the משנה says 'four or five baskets,' does it mean exactly four or five baskets and no more? That would show that cutting down on walking matters most. Or maybe cutting down on how heavy each load is matters most, so you could use more, smaller baskets?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an איבעיא about how to read the 'four or five baskets' limit in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clearing a room on שבת is extra effort (טרחא), so the משנה puts a limit on it. One reading: count the baskets, meaning fewer, heavier trips (less walking). Other reading: the limit is about total amount, so you may split it into many lighter baskets (less burden each time).

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked of them (an open question the Sages tried to settle)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that the total amount is about five big baskets' worth. The question is only whether you may break it into more, lighter trips.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
These four or five baskets that the משנה mentioned,
phrases.notes: Referring to the משנה's permission to clear baskets for guests.

phrases.english: in four or five baskets, yes,
more, no?
This would show that cutting down the walking is better.
Or perhaps cutting down the load is better.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question on the משנה's 'four or five baskets,' after the side discussion about the measure of piled grain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the limit restrict the number of baskets (fewer trips), or does it allow more, lighter baskets as long as the total stays the same?

steps.title: Trying to prove it from two ברייתות that give different numbers
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says four or five baskets, another says ten or fifteen; the גמרא suggests they argue about exactly this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One ברייתא teaches that you may clear even four or five baskets of oil jugs and wine jugs. Another ברייתא says ten and fifteen. Isn't it that they argue about this? One Sage holds that fewer trips is better, and the other holds that lighter loads are better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to settle the question by pointing to two ברייתות with different numbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that 'four or five' fits the view that fewer trips is better, while 'ten or fifteen' baskets fits the view that more, lighter loads is better. If so, the question is a real argument between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that…? (proposes a reading)

phrases.english: Come and hear, for one ברייתא teaches:
One may clear out even four or five baskets

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל כַּדֵּי שֶׁמֶן וְשֶׁל כַּדֵּי יַיִן.
phrases.english: of jugs of oil and of jugs of wine.
And another ברייתא teaches: in ten and in fifteen.
Is it not that they argue about this:
that one Sage holds cutting down the walking is better,
and the other Sage holds cutting down the load is better?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a source-based answer to the question in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of walking vs. load is a real argument between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות, one allowing four or five baskets and one allowing ten or fifteen.

steps.title: Rejected: the larger numbers count jugs, not baskets
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees fewer trips is better; 'ten and fifteen' counts jugs packed two or three per basket, like the small jugs of הרפניא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that fewer trips is better. Do you think 'ten and fifteen' means baskets? It means jugs. So there is no contradiction: one ברייתא is where one jug fits in each basket, one is where two fit, and one is where three fit, such as the small jugs of הרפניא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by reading the second ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Ten and fifteen' counts jugs, not baskets. The number of baskets is always five: five baskets hold five, ten, or fifteen jugs depending on jug size. So both ברייתות agree that cutting down trips is what matters.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you think…? (signals a misreading)
And it is not a contradiction
Small jugs from the town of הרפניא

steps.whatToRemember: The limit is five baskets (counting trips), not a total weight. You may not split the load into many lighter trips. The higher numbers in the ברייתא count small jugs inside those same five baskets.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the main concern with clearing on שבת is how much walking back and forth one does.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מַעוֹטֵי בְּהִילּוּכָא עֲדִיף,
phrases.english: No, everyone agrees that cutting down the walking is better.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי סָבְרַתְּ ״בְּעֶשֶׂר וּבַחֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה״ אַקּוּפּוֹת קָאֵי?
phrases.english: And do you think 'in ten and in fifteen' refers to baskets?
It refers to jugs, and there is no contradiction:
this one is where they are carried one by one in a basket,
and this one is where they are carried two by two,
and this one is where they are carried three by three,
such as with the small jugs of Harpanya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 15 by rereading the second ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the two ברייתות argue; it does not reject the ברייתות themselves.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'ten and fifteen' counts baskets, but it counts jugs inside five baskets.

steps.title: Does the limit grow when there are more guests?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether four or five baskets is the limit even with many guests, or whether it depends on how many guests there are.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: The 'four or five' that the משנה mentions, does it apply even if he has many guests? Or maybe it all depends on how many guests there are?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new איבעיא about whether the number of guests changes the limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side: four or five is a fixed cap, no matter how many guests come. Other side: the amount depends on the need, so more guests allow more clearing.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
These four or five that the משנה mentioned,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית לֵיהּ אוֹרְחִין טוּבָא,
phrases.english: do they apply even though he has many guests?
Or perhaps it all depends on the number of guests?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question on the same משנה after the walking vs. load question was settled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the four or five basket limit fixed, or does it change with the number of guests?

steps.title: If it depends on the guests, who does the clearing?
steps.stepSummary: If the amount grows with the guests, does one person clear for all of them, or does each guest clear for himself?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it all depends on the number of guests, does one man clear space for all of them? Or perhaps each man clears space for himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a follow-up question that only applies if the answer to the first question is 'it depends on the guests.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ואם תמצי לומר' mean 'if you answer the first side.' Then a new detail is asked: may one person do all the extra clearing for many guests? Or is each person limited to clearing his own share?

keyTerms.meaning: And if you conclude (introduces a follow-up question)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a separate question standing alone. It only matters if the limit really depends on the number of guests.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר הַכֹּל לְפִי הָאוֹרְחִין,
phrases.english: And if you say it all depends on the number of guests,
does one man clear space for all of them,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא גַּבְרָא גַּבְרָא מְפַנֵּי לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ?
phrases.english: or perhaps each man clears space for himself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question built on one side of step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If clearing grows with the guests, may one person clear for everyone, or must each person clear only for himself?

steps.title: רבי cleared a whole field for his students
steps.stepSummary: Answering the question from step 17, the גמרא quotes רבה in the name of רבי חייא: רבי found the place too crowded for his students and cleared an entire field full of sheaves. This suggests the amount depends on the number of guests.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבה said in the name of רבי חייא: Once רבי went to a certain place and saw that it was too crowded for the students. He went out to a field, found it full of sheaves, and cleared the entire field. (Learn from this: it all depends on the number of guests.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from step 17 with a story. רבי cleared a whole field of sheaves because he had many students to fit in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה allowed four or five baskets. Clearing a whole field is far more than that, so the limit must grow when there are more guests. The many students are what justified the large amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to answer a question
Learn from this: a conclusion drawn from a source

steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה. He is a different person from רבי חייא, who is only the one telling the story here. Note also that the closing line 'שמע מינה' appears in parentheses in this version. It is written in full after the second version below.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
for Rabba said that Rabbi Chiya said:

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת הָלַךְ רַבִּי לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Once Rabbi went to a certain place,
and saw that the place was too crowded for the students,
and he went out to the field
and found a field full of sheaves,
and Rabbi cleared the sheaves from the entire field.
phrases.notes: He cleared the space on שבת to make room for the students.

phrases.english: (Learn from this: it all depends on the number of guests.)

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question from step 17: is there a fixed limit, or does it depend on the guests?
steps.raayaObject: The amount one may clear is not fixed. It depends on how many guests there are.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story told by רבה in the name of רבי חייא about רבי clearing a whole field.

steps.title: Second version: רבי חייא cleared the field
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, quoting רבי הושעיא, tells the same story but says it was רבי חייא who cleared the field. The same conclusion follows: the amount depends on the number of guests.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said in the name of רבי הושעיא: Once רבי חייא went to a certain place and saw that it was too crowded for the students. He went out to a field, found it full of sheaves, and cleared the entire field. Learn from this: it all depends on the number of guests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same story. Here the person who cleared the field was רבי חייא, not רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only difference is who did the clearing. In both versions, a whole field was cleared because there were many students. So either way, the rule is 'הכל לפי האורחין': the amount follows the number of guests.

keyTerms.meaning: The entire field, all of it

steps.whatToRemember: Conclusion of the question from step 17: הכל לפי האורחין. The more guests there are, the more one may clear.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said that Rabbi Hoshaya said:

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת הָלַךְ רַבִּי חִיָּיא לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: Once Rabbi Chiya went to a certain place
and saw that the place was too crowded for the students,
and he went out to the field
and found a field full of sheaves,

phrases.aramaic: וְעִימֵּר רַבִּי חִיָּיא כׇּל הַשָּׂדֶה כּוּלָּהּ.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Chiya cleared the sheaves from the entire field.
Learn from this: it all depends on the number of guests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel version of the story in step 19, with a different person doing the clearing. It leads to the same conclusion.
steps.raayaObject: The amount one may clear depends on the number of guests.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story told by רב יוסף in the name of רבי הושעיא about רבי חייא clearing a whole field.

steps.title: Who does the clearing: one person or each guest?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the amount depends on the guests, the גמרא repeats the open question from step 18. Does one person clear for everyone, or does each guest clear his own space?
steps.simpleTranslation: And you can still ask: Does one man clear for all of them, or perhaps each and every man clears for himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The first question is settled, but the גמרא says the second question from step 18 is still open. Who actually does the clearing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one person may clear for everyone, he could move a very large amount by himself. If each guest must clear his own space, then each person moves only what he personally needs. The stories did not clearly settle this.

keyTerms.meaning: And still you can ask: the question remains open

phrases.english: And you can still ask:
Does one man clear for all of them,
or perhaps each and every man
clears for himself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first question is resolved, so the גמרא returns to the follow-up question from step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one person may clear for all the guests, or each guest clears only his own space.

steps.title: Proof from the words 'רבי cleared'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a proof from the story's wording, 'וְעִימֵּר רַבִּי'. Since רבי did the clearing, it seems one person may clear for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And רבי cleared.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the new question from the wording of the story. It says that רבי, one person, cleared the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story says רבי himself cleared the field for all his students. If that is meant literally, one person cleared for many, which would answer the question that one man may clear for all.

keyTerms.meaning: And רבי cleared: the exact wording being used as proof
רבי יהודה הנשיא, the leader of his generation

phrases.english: Come and hear: "And Rabbi cleared."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer step 21's question using the wording of the story in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: One person may clear for all the guests.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording 'וְעִימֵּר רַבִּי' in the story from step 19.

steps.title: רבי gave the order; each person cleared for himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי, the great leader, would not have cleared the sheaves with his own hands. He ordered others to do it, so it is called his clearing. It is still possible that each person cleared his own space.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, did רבי clear the sheaves himself?! Rather, he commanded, and that is why it says he 'cleared.' And really, each and every one clears for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. 'רבי cleared' only means he gave the instructions, so the story does not show that one person cleared for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on reading 'רבי cleared' literally. But a leader like רבי would not do such work himself. The words mean he ordered it, and the students may each have cleared their own place, so the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turning the questioner's logic back on him
By himself, with his own hands

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'וְעִימֵּר רַבִּי' as if רבי physically moved the sheaves. The גמרא explains it means he gave the order. Something done on a person's instruction is often described as if he did it himself.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof that one person clears for all is rejected. 'וְעִימֵּר רַבִּי' only means רבי gave the order. The גמרא's closing words, 'ולעולם כל חד וחד מפני לנפשיה', belong to this rejection: it is still possible that each guest cleared his own space, so the story does not show that one man may clear for everyone.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
did Rabbi clear the sheaves himself?!
phrases.notes: It is unthinkable that the leader of the generation did this physical work himself.

phrases.english: Rather, he commanded, and so it is called his clearing,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְעוֹלָם כׇּל חַד וְחַד מְפַנֵּי לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ.
phrases.english: and really, each and every one clears for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 22 by reading 'רבי cleared' as 'רבי ordered the clearing.'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the wording. It does not reject the story's main lesson that the amount depends on the guests.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'עימר' means רבי did the work himself. In fact it means he commanded it, so nothing shows that one person cleared for all.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof that one man clears for everyone is rejected, since 'ועימר רבי' can mean he ordered it and each student cleared his own place.

steps.title: Welcoming guests equals coming early to the study hall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'מפני האורחין'. רבי יוחנן learns that הכנסת אורחין is as great as השכמת בית המדרש, because the משנה lists the two side by side.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Because of the guests,' etc. רבי יוחנן said: Welcoming guests is as great as coming early to the study hall. We know this because the משנה teaches the two together: 'because of the guests and because of stopping the learning in the study hall.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase from the משנה and starts a new topic about how great it is to welcome guests. רבי יוחנן learns from the משנה that welcoming guests and Torah learning in the בית המדרש are equally important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows extra work on שבת, moving baskets of produce, for two reasons: guests and the בית המדרש. Since the משנה uses both reasons to permit the same thing, רבי יוחנן learns that the two are equal in importance.

keyTerms.meaning: Coming early to the study hall to learn Torah
The learning in the study hall being stopped

phrases.english: [The mishnah taught:] 'Because of the guests,' etc.
phrases.notes: A quote of the opening words of the משנה, used to start a new discussion

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Great is welcoming guests
like coming early to the study hall,
as it teaches: 'Because of the guests'
'and because of stopping the learning in the study hall.'
phrases.notes: The two reasons are listed together, so they are treated as equal

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי הָאוֹרְחִין וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the practical question of clearing space and opens a teaching about the value of guests, based on the same phrase of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הכנסת אורחין is equal in greatness to השכמת בית המדרש

steps.title: Welcoming guests is even greater than the study hall
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי מנהרדעא says הכנסת אורחין is greater than השכמת בית המדרש, because the משנה mentions guests first and only afterward the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי from נהרדעא said: Welcoming guests is greater than coming early to the study hall. We know this because the משנה first says 'because of the guests' and only afterward says 'and because of stopping the learning in the study hall.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion reads the same משנה differently. רב דימי says guests come first in the משנה, so they are more important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן looked at the fact that the two reasons appear together. רב דימי looks at their order, and since guests are listed first, he concludes that guests are ranked higher.

keyTerms.meaning: Neharde'a, a major Torah city in Babylonia

phrases.english: And Rav Dimi from Neharde'a said:
[It is] greater than coming early to the study hall,
as it teaches 'because of the guests' [first],
and only afterward 'and because of stopping the learning in the study hall.'
phrases.notes: The order shows which one is more important

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing reading of the same משנה, based on order rather than on the two reasons being listed together
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הכנסת אורחין is greater than השכמת בית המדרש

steps.title: Welcoming guests is greater than greeting the Divine Presence
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, says הכנסת אורחין is greater than receiving the שכינה. אברהם asked ה׳ to wait for him while he took care of his guests.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Welcoming guests is greater than receiving the שכינה. This is because the פסוק says: 'And he said: My Lord, if I have found favor in Your eyes, please do not pass on' from Your servant.
steps.whatsHappening: רב goes even further than the earlier opinions. He proves from אברהם that welcoming guests is greater than standing before the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ was appearing to אברהם when the three guests arrived. אברהם asked ה׳ to 'not pass on,' meaning to wait, while he ran to serve the guests. Since he put the guests ahead of the שכינה, hosting guests must be even greater.

keyTerms.meaning: Receiving or greeting the Divine Presence
As it is written (in a פסוק)
Please do not pass on (please wait)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Welcoming guests is greater
than receiving the Divine Presence,
as it is written: 'And he said: My Lord,'
'if now I have found favor in Your eyes,'
'please do not pass on, etc.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:3. אברהם asks ה׳ to wait while he serves the guests

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב גְּדוֹלָה הַכְנָסַת אוֹרְחִין מֵהַקְבָּלַת פְּנֵי שְׁכִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the importance of hosting guests even higher, using a פסוק instead of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הכנסת אורחין is greater than הקבלת פני שכינה

steps.title: God's way is unlike the way of human beings
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points out that among people, a lesser person cannot ask a greater person to wait for him. Yet אברהם asked ה׳ to wait, and ה׳ agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Come and see that the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא is not like the way of human beings. Among human beings, a lesser person cannot say to a greater person, 'Wait until I come to you.' But about הקדוש ברוך הוא it is written: 'And he said: My Lord, if I have found favor, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר uses the same פסוק to teach a lesson about ה׳ Himself. ה׳ is humble enough to wait for a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב used the פסוק to show how great guests are. רבי אלעזר uses it to show something about ה׳: no human king would wait for a lesser person, but ה׳ waited for אברהם.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and see (a phrase that introduces a lesson)
The way of flesh and blood, meaning human beings
A lesser person / a greater person

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Come and see that not like the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood.
The way of flesh and blood [is that]
a lesser person cannot say to a greater person
'Wait until I come to you,'
whereas regarding the Holy One, Blessed be He, it is written
'And he said: My Lord, if now I have found [favor], etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a second lesson from the same פסוק, this time about ה׳'s humility
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ waits for a lesser being, which human beings of high rank do not do

steps.title: Six מצוות whose fruits are eaten in this world
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן lists six things whose 'fruits' a person enjoys in this world while the 'principal' stays for עולם הבא. Welcoming guests is first on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר שילא said in the name of רבי אסי, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: There are six things whose fruits a person eats in this world while the principal stays for him in עולם הבא. They are: welcoming guests, visiting the sick, concentrating in prayer, coming early to the study hall, raising one's sons to learn Torah, and judging another person favorably.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the praise of guests, the גמרא brings a list of six special מצוות, and welcoming guests is one of them. For each one, a person gets reward now and still keeps the main reward for later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The picture is an investment. You get the 'interest' (fruits) in this world, and the 'principal' (the main reward) stays untouched for עולם הבא. The list includes השכמת בית המדרש next to הכנסת אורחין, which matches the earlier discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: Their fruits, meaning the benefit or 'interest' in this world
The principal remains, meaning the main reward is kept
Careful focus and concentration in prayer
Judging others favorably (giving them the benefit of the doubt)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Sheila said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים אָדָם אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹתֵיהֶן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: Six things a person eats their fruits in this world
and the principal remains for him for the World-to-Come,
and these are they: welcoming guests,
and visiting the sick, and concentration in prayer,
and coming early to the study hall,
and one who raises his sons to Torah study,
and one who judges his fellow favorably.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the praise of הכנסת אורחין by placing it in a list of מצוות with double reward
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six מצוות, including הכנסת אורחין, give fruits in this world while the principal stays for עולם הבא
steps.whyThisMatters: This list will now be challenged, and the challenge shapes how we understand which מצוות carry this double reward.

steps.title: Challenge from a משנה with a different list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן can list these six, when a משנה lists other מצוות for this reward and seems to say that only those count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But we learned in a משנה: These are the things that a person does and eats their fruits in this world, while the principal stays for him in עולם הבא: honoring father and mother, acts of kindness, bringing peace between a person and his friend, and Torah study is equal to all of them. This implies that these, yes, and other things, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's list of six with a משנה (in מסכת פאה) that gives a different list. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה opens with 'אלו', meaning 'these are,' which sounds like a complete and closed list. Most of רבי יוחנן's six items, such as visiting the sick, are not mentioned in it. So the משנה seems to exclude them.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not that רבי יוחנן's items are bad מצוות. The question is only whether the משנה's list is meant to be complete. If it is, how can there be other items with this same reward?

phrases.english: Is that so?! But we learned [in a mishnah]:
These are the things that a person does them
and eats their fruits in this world,
and the principal remains for him for the World-to-Come,
and these are they: honoring father and mother,
and acts of loving kindness,
and bringing peace between a person and his fellow,
and Torah study is equal to all of them
[These, yes,
other things, no]!
phrases.notes: This is what the גמרא learns from the word 'אלו'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's list of six from step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's list of six מצוות that bear fruits in this world
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives a different list that sounds closed ('these, yes; others, no'), so additional items like visiting the sick should not have this reward
